label: thm:ftc1
title: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement: Let $f$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ and $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$. Then $F(u) = \int_a^u f(t)\,dt$ satisfies $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; F\; (f\; x)\; x$. The core Mathlib result is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}.
proof: We verify the three hypotheses of \texttt{integral\_hasDerivAt\_right}: (1) interval integrability on $[a,x]$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:interval_integrable_restriction}; (2) strong measurability at $\texttt{nhds}\;x$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:strongly_measurable_interior}; (3) continuity at $x$ via Lemma~\ref{lem:continuous_at_interior}.
